questions.stem: An account earns an annual effective interest rate of 10%. Calculate the nominal annual interest rate compounded monthly that is equivalent to this effective rate.
A 16-year bond with face amount 1,000 pays annual coupons at a rate of 6% and is redeemable at par. Calculate the price to yield an annual effective rate of 5%.
A loan of 20,000 is amortized with level annual payments over 20 years at an annual effective rate of 8%. Calculate the outstanding loan balance immediately after the 14th payment.
questions.solution:
First find the level payment: PMT = Loan / a(20|i) = 20,000 / 9.81815 = 2,037.04.
By the prospective method, the balance after payment 14 is the present value of the remaining 6 payments:
OB = PMT x a(6|0.08) = 2,037.04 x 4.62288 = 9,417.01.

questions.stem: A cash flow stream pays 1 at the end of each year for 8 years. Using an annual effective interest rate of 6%, calculate the Macaulay duration of the stream.
questions.solution:
Macaulay duration = [sum t v^t CF_t] / [sum v^t CF_t].
Numerator = 26.05137, Denominator = 6.20979
D = 4.1952 years.

questions.stem: An annuity pays 300 at the end of year 1, 600 at the end of year 2, increasing by 300 each year, for 7 years. At an annual effective rate of 5%, calculate the present value.
A payment of 10,000 will be received 7 years from now. Using an annual effective interest rate of 8.0%, calculate the present value of this payment.
A 14-year, 1,000 par bond pays 6% annual coupons and is bought to yield 4% annual effective. Calculate the amount of premium in the purchase price.
questions.solution:
Since the coupon rate exceeds the yield, the bond sells at a premium.
Price = Fr x a(n|i) + C v^n = 60.00 x 10.56312 + 1,000 x 0.57748 = 1,211.26
Premium = Price - Redemption = 1,211.26 - 1,000 = 211.26.

questions.stem: A loan of 25,000 is repaid with level annual payments over 15 years at 7% annual effective. Calculate the interest portion of the 5th payment.
An annuity pays 1,000 at the end of each year for 25 years. Using an annual effective interest rate of 6%, calculate the present value of the annuity.
Deposits of 500 are made at the BEGINNING of each year for 6 years into a fund earning an annual effective rate of 6%. Calculate the accumulated value of the fund at the end of 6 years.
A perpetuity pays 50 at the end of each year forever. Using an annual effective interest rate of 4%, calculate its present value.
questions.solution:
A perpetuity-immediate has PV = PMT / i.
PV = 50 / 0.04 = 1,250.00.

questions.stem: A fund begins the year with 10,000. A deposit of 8,000 is made at mid-year. The fund balance at year-end is 19,500. Using the dollar-weighted (simple interest) method, calculate the annual yield rate.
questions.solution:
Interest earned I = End - Begin - Deposits = 19,500 - 10,000 - 8,000 = 1,500.
Dollar-weighted yield i = I / (A + sum C_t (1 - t)).
i = 1,500 / (10,000 + 8,000 x 0.5) = 1,500 / 14,000.00 = 10.714%.

questions.stem: A loan of 10,000 is repaid with level annual payments at the end of each year for 13 years. The annual effective interest rate is 6%. Calculate the annual payment.
An investment of 3,000 is made in a fund that earns an annual effective interest rate of 7.0%. Calculate the accumulated value of the fund at the end of 15 years.
questions.solution:
The accumulated value uses AV = PV(1 + i)^n.
AV = 3,000 x (1 + 0.070)^15
AV = 3,000 x 2.75903
AV = 8,277.09.

questions.solution:
The accumulated value uses AV = PV(1 + i)^n.
AV = 500 x (1 + 0.040)^12
AV = 500 x 1.60103
AV = 800.52.

Interest earned I = End - Begin - Deposits = 13,500 - 10,000 - 2,000 = 1,500.
